# Claims and Contribution Record — TEMPLATE ONLY

## Inherited foundations and prior art

List conventional objects, algorithms, equations, theories, sources, and known related work. Cite their original authors and established domain literature when possible.

## The particular BFL addition

Name exactly what was reconstructed, integrated, represented, implemented, or newly demonstrated. Separate expressive authorship from originality of the underlying mathematical ideas.

## Claims and their maturity

For each substantive claim: ID, wording, type (definition / hypothesis / theorem / bounded test / negative result), assumptions, evidence, counterevidence, verification scope, and limitations.

## Comparative baseline

Describe the native-domain method or existing software that could already solve the same problem. A simpler baseline winning is a valid result.

## Known defects and open obligations

Preserve failed cases, rejected hypotheses, missing sources, unverified claims, and the next discriminating check.

## Source and legal boundary

Point to cleared sources, link to the governing project release metadata, identify third-party material, and make no blanket rights statement. A bibliography does not itself grant redistribution rights.
